title: Algebra
tagline: Equations, progressions, and the binomial — patterns, not brute force.

subsections.title: Linear Equations in Two Variables
subsections.trick: Compare a/p, b/q, c/r before touching algebra — the ratio pattern tells you instantly whether it's one line, no solution, or a unique solution, without solving anything.

pyqs.q: Given a−6b+6c=4 and 6a+3b−3c=50, find 2a+3b−3c.
pyqs.a: Group (b−c) as a single variable u: a−6u=4 and 6a+3u=50. Double the first equation's u-coefficient to match by scaling the second: 12a+6u=100; add to the first → 13a=104 → a=8, then 3u=2. So 2a+3u = 16+2 = ×18.

subsections.title: Binomial Theorem
subsections.trick: The (r+1)th term formula is your entry point for every ‘find the coefficient of x^k’ question — set the exponent of x equal to k and solve for r first, then plug back in.

pyqs.q: Find the term independent of x in the expansion of (x + 2/x²)¹⁵.
pyqs.a: General term: Tᵣ₊₁ = ¹⁵Cᵣ x^(15−r) (2/x²)ʳ = ¹⁵Cᵣ 2ʳ x^(15−3r). Term is independent of x when 15−3r=0 → r=5. So the term is ¹⁵C₅ × 2⁵ — set r from the exponent equation first, then plug in; don't expand the whole binomial.

subsections.title: Quadratic Equations
subsections.trick: Almost every CAT quadratic question wants sum/product of roots, not the roots themselves — use −b/a and c/a directly and skip the quadratic formula entirely. For max/min of ax²+bx+c, the vertex x = −b/2a is also the average of the two roots. If roots differ by a fixed amount k, square it: (α−β)² = (α+β)² − 4αβ = k² — turns a 'roots differ by...' question into one substitution.

pyqs.q: Find the number of non-negative integer values of k for which x²−5x+k=0 has only integer roots.
pyqs.a: Sum of roots is fixed at 5 (Vieta's). Since k=αβ≥0 and α+β=5>0, both roots must be non-negative integers. List pairs summing to 5: (0,5),(1,4),(2,3) → k=0,4,6 — ×3 values.

pyqs.q: 3x²−5x+p=0 and 2x²−2x+q=0 share exactly one root. Find the sum of the other two (non-common) roots.
pyqs.a: Write both equations' root-sum relations and eliminate the common root by combining them (multiply to match coefficients, subtract). The non-common roots' sum comes out to ×−⅔p+³⁄₂q.

pyqs.q: Roots of x²−px+q=0 are real and differ by exactly 1. Which relation must hold?
pyqs.a: Shortcut: just invent a matching pair, e.g. roots 2 and 3 → x²−5x+6=0, so p=5, q=6. Test p²=4q+1: 25 = 24+1 ✓. — 15 seconds beats deriving (α−β)²=(α+β)²−4αβ from scratch under time pressure. Answer: ×p² = 4q+1.

pyqs.q: f(x) = (x²+3x)(x²+3x+2). Find the sum of all real roots of f(x)+11 = 970.
pyqs.a: Substitute y = x²+3x: y(y+2)+11 = 970 → y²+2y−959 = 0 → (y+32)(y−30)=0. Only y=30 gives real x (y=−32 has negative discriminant for x). x²+3x−30=0 → sum of roots = −b/a = ×−3.

pyqs.q: Find a c for which min of f(x)=x²−4cx+8c exceeds max of g(x)=−x²+3cx−2c.
pyqs.a: Use the vertex formulas directly: fₘᵢₙ = −4c²+8c (at x=2c), gₘₐₓ = ⁹⁄₄c²−2c (at x=³⁄₂c). Setting fₘᵢₙ > gₘₐₓ gives 0 < c < 1.6 — any option in that range works, e.g. ×c = ½.

subsections.title: Cubic & Higher Degree Equations
subsections.trick: The sign of each root-sum formula alternates: +, +, − for a cubic’s three symmetric sums. Remainder Theorem (plug in x=a) is almost always faster than long division for ‘is (x−a) a factor’ questions.

pyqs.q: P(x)=x⁴−2x³+ax²+bx+8 leaves remainder 5 on division by (x−1) and 20 by (x+2). Find a+b.
pyqs.a: Remainder Theorem, one substitution: P(1)=5 → 1−2+a+b+8=5 → ×a+b = −2. (You don't even need the second condition unless asked for a and b individually.)

subsections.title: AP, GP & HP
subsections.trick: If a question mixes three numbers in AP, GP and HP, remember (GM)² = AM × HM — it often replaces two equations with one. For GP sums, check r<1 vs r>1 before picking the formula, and don’t forget the infinite-sum formula only applies for |r|<1.

formulas.label: GP — sum of n terms, r<1
GP — sum of n terms, r>1

pyqs.q: A decreasing infinite GP has a₁+a₂+a₃=52 and a₁a₂+a₂a₃+a₃a₁=624. Find the sum to infinity.
pyqs.a: Solve the two symmetric equations for a₁=36, r=⅓. Sum to infinity = 36/(1−⅓) = ×54.

pyqs.q: In an AP, t₄+t₇+t₁₀=99 and S₁₄=497. Find S₅.
pyqs.a: t₄+t₇+t₁₀ = 3a+18d = 99 → a+6d=33. S₁₄ = 7(2a+13d)=497 → 2a+13d=71. Solve simultaneously: d=5, a=3 → S₅ = ⁵⁄₂(2×3+4×5) = ×65.

pyqs.q: In {1,3,5,...,57}, find k such that the sum of elements below k equals the sum of elements above k.
pyqs.a: Odd numbers up to the m-th term sum to m² — use that identity instead of summing manually. With 29 total terms (sum=29²=841), set (m−1)² = 841−m² → m(m−1)=420=21×20 → m=21 → k=2(21)−1 = ×41.

pyqs.q: aₖ=3ᵏ. Find the smallest m for which (a₁)¹(a₂)²⋯(a₂₀)²⁰ < a₂₁a₂₂⋯a₂₀₊ₘ.
pyqs.a: Compare exponents only (same base 3): LHS exponent = Σk² for k=1..20 = 20·21·41/6 = 2870. RHS exponent = Σ from 21 to 20+m = m(41+m)/2. Need m(m+41) > 5740; testing m=58 gives 58×99=5742 (works), m=57 gives 5586 (fails) → ×m = 58.

subsections.title: Logarithms
subsections.trick: Change of base (formula 10) is the escape hatch whenever a log question mixes different bases — route everything through a common base and the rest collapses. Base 10 is the default unless stated otherwise.

pyqs.q: Solve log₃x + log₉x + log₂₇x = 11.
pyqs.a: Shortcut: since bases are powers of 3, guess x is a power of 3 and test options directly. x=3⁶=729: log₃(3⁶)+log₃²(3⁶)+log₃³(3⁶) = 6+3+2 = 11 ✓ in under 10 seconds. Answer: ×729.

pyqs.q: Find the number of distinct integers n for which log₂(¼ + 1/(117n)) > 0.
pyqs.a: Removing the log: ¼ + 1/(117n) > 1 needs 1/(117n) > ¾, which forces n to be a tiny positive fraction — no integer n works, and checking the domain (argument > 0) for negative n never pushes the sum above 1 either. Answer: ×0 integers.

pyqs.q: log₆₄x + log₈y + log₂z = 4. Find the minimum possible value of (x+y+z).
pyqs.a: Convert every term to base 2: ⁱ⁄₆log₂x + ⁱ⁄₃log₂y + log₂z = 4 → x^(1/6)y^(1/3)z = 16. Apply weighted AM-GM with weights 1/6, 1/3, 1 (summing to 3/2) on x, y, z to get the minimum sum directly: ×24.

subsections.title: Algebraic Manipulation — x + 1/x Family
subsections.trick: Every power sum xⁿ+1/xⁿ builds from the one below it — never expand from scratch. Get (x+1/x), then square/cube it to reach x²+1/x² and x³+1/x³, then multiply pairs of known power-sums together to reach higher ones.

pyqs.q: Given x²+1/x² = 25 for x > 0, find x⁷+1/x⁷.
pyqs.a: x+1/x = √27 = 3√3. Then x³+1/x³ = (3√3)³−3(3√3) = 18√3, and x⁴+1/x⁴ = 25²−2 = 623. Multiply the 3rd and 4th power-sums and subtract the 1st: (18√3)(623) − 3√3 = ×344,856.

subsections.title: Functions, Domain/Range & Inequalities
subsections.trick: For range-of-a-rational-function questions, set y=f(x), cross-multiply into a quadratic in x, and demand discriminant ≥0 — this converts almost any range question into a simple quadratic inequality in y. For integer-count inequality questions, fix the smaller variable and count the window for the other one, rather than searching blindly.

formulas.label: Range of a rational function via discriminant

pyqs.q: Find the number of integer pairs (x,y) with x > y ≥ 3 and x+y < 14.
pyqs.a: Fix y and count the valid x window for each: y=3→7 values, y=4→5, y=5→3, y=6→1. Total = 7+5+3+1 = ×16 pairs.

pyqs.q: For 3≤x≤6, find the set where [x²] = [x]² (greatest integer function).
pyqs.a: Break into unit intervals by [x]: on [3,4), need 9≤x²<10 → x∈[3,√10); similarly [4,5)→[4,√17), [5,6)→[5,√26); and x=6 works exactly. Union these interval pieces — don't try to solve it as one continuous inequality.

pyqs.q: Find real x satisfying x²−|x+9|+x > 0.
pyqs.a: Split strictly at the sign-change point x=−9, not at 0. For x≥−9: reduces to x²−9>0 → x∈(−9,−3)∪(3,∞). For x<−9: reduces to x²+2x+9>0, true everywhere (discriminant<0). Union: ×(−∞,−3)∪(3,∞).

pyqs.q: f(x)=x/(2x−1), g(x)=x/(x−1). Find points excluded from the domain of h(x)=f(g(x))+g(f(x)).
pyqs.a: Track every denominator that can hit zero through the composition (x−1 in g, 2x−1 in f, and whatever makes the composed denominators vanish) — gives the excluded set ×{−1, ½, 1}.

pyqs.q: Integers a,b,c,d sum to 46. Find the minimum possible (a−b)²+(a−c)²+(a−d)².
pyqs.a: Sum-of-squared-differences is minimized by making all four values as close to equal as possible (46/4=11.5 → use 12,12,11,11). If a itself can be chosen equal to b,c,d it drops to ×0 — check exactly what the question fixes before assuming a nonzero answer.

pyqs.q: Find the range of f(x) = (2x²−4x+6)/(x²−2x+4) for real x.
Naturals p,q,r sum to 900; r is a perfect square with 150<r<500; 0.3q≤p≤0.7q. Find (p_max + p_min).
pyqs.a: With S=900−r, the bounds become ³⁄₁³S ≤ p ≤ ⁷⁄₁₇S. r ranges over perfect squares strictly between 150 and 500, i.e. 13² through 22² (169 to 484). p is maximised when r is smallest (r=169, S=731 → p=⌊⁷⁄₁₇×731⌋=301) and minimised when r is largest (r=484, S=416 → p=⌈³⁄₁³×416⌉=96). Sum = ×397.
